title: Data-based analysis of hypotension prevalence and management in the clinical context of intensive care units
summary:
Sufficient blood flow to vital organs plays an important role in intensive care medicine. However, the blood flow to tissues cannot be measured directly at the patient's bedside. Instead, the mean arterial blood pressure (MAP) is used as a substitute value. Hypotension is typically assumed if this value falls below 65 mmHg. Such drops in blood pressure lead, for example, to essential organs not being adequately supplied with oxygen, which in turn can lead to serious consequences such as kidney damage or a higher risk of death.

This study retrospectively analyzes blood pressure data from patients treated in various intensive care units at the University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein (Campus Lübeck). The data is collected through routine patient monitoring. Typical patterns of hypotension are to be described and evaluated using various parameters that represent the duration, depth, and frequency of blood pressure drops. A further aim of the study is to utilize these parameters for clustering methods, i.e., machine learning methods for organizing data points into groups, to identify patients with comparable blood pressure patterns. It will also investigate whether blood pressure drops and specific patterns of them occur more frequently in some intensive care units or are related to a short or longer stay in intensive care. The results should help to understand blood pressure patterns better and, if necessary, improve the management of hypotension in intensive care units.

interventions.name: All patients who were admitted to one of the three participating intensive care units at the University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Lübeck, during the study period and for whom continuous mean arterial pressure data are available in the Philips Data Warehouse will be included.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Availability of continuously recorded mean arterial pressure during the stay in one of the participating intensive care units.
Exclusion criteria:
Apart from the absence of continuously recorded arterial pressure data, no further exclusion criteria are defined.
